summary: Extend the existing vanilla-JS static frontend instead of rebuilding it. Preserve clipboard parsing, 6-candidate compact previews, candidate selection, and two-click swap editing. Replace the old role-preference order model with a per-player `6점 분배` model, migrate saved data safely, simplify the saved-player library to a name-first exact-10 selector with delete actions, and keep balance-score numbers hidden while preserving the mandated candidate ranking order.

milestones.title: Preference Model Migration
milestones.objective: Convert the runtime and persistence model from ranked role order to integer role-preference points while keeping the current 10-player balance flow intact.
deliverables: Update `src/types.ts` so `MatchPlayer`, `SavedPlayerRecord`, slot metadata, and helper types use `preferencePoints: { tank, damage, support }` instead of `preferenceOrder`.

Replace order-based helpers in `src/lib/preferences.js` with point-based helpers: default `2/2/2`, integer clamping, sum-to-6 normalization, legacy order-to-points migration, and assigned-role fit metadata generation.
Refactor `src/lib/appFlow.js` so pasted players, loaded saved players, candidate hydration, and editor refresh all read/write `preferencePoints` as part of canonical `matchPlayers` state.
Keep clipboard parsing in `src/lib/parseClipboard.js` at the existing 4-column TSV shape with optional header support; role-preference points remain UI-managed state, not pasted input columns.

Introduce backward-compatible saved-data migration in `src/lib/playerStore.js`: load new schema first, fall back to current v1 payloads, and convert legacy `preferenceOrder` records into point distributions without crashing or dropping records.

milestones.title: Roster Editing UX
milestones.objective: Give the user a simple Korean UI to adjust each active player's role-preference points while guaranteeing the three-role sum always remains 6.
deliverables: Replace the current `1순위 / 2순위 / 3순위` controls in `src/lib/render.js` and `src/styles.css` with compact per-role integer controls for `탱커 / 딜러 / 힐러` in the current-roster section.

Use constrained steppers or equivalent normalized controls in `src/main.js` so each edit updates one role and rebalances the other two through shared helper logic; runtime state must never store a non-integer or a total other than 6.
Set the default preference distribution for new players to `탱커 2 / 딜러 2 / 힐러 2` unless a saved record already exists for that player.
Refresh preview, candidate metadata, and editor metadata immediately after a preference edit, while continuing to hide personal/team balance-score numbers from the main result UI.
Update Korean product copy in `src/constants/copy.js` so the roster section clearly explains that preference points are a soft signal and not a hard override of tier balance.

milestones.title: Saved Player Library Simplification
milestones.objective: Keep local saved-player workflows, but simplify the browsing UI to a name-first list and add deletion management.
deliverables: Refactor the saved-player panel in `src/lib/render.js` and `src/styles.css` from card-heavy layout to a simple name-centered list row with checkbox, player name, minimal secondary summary, and per-row delete action.
Extend `src/lib/playerStore.js` with individual delete and clear-all helpers, plus safe persistence after each mutation.
Update `src/main.js` state and event binding so saved-player selection count, exact-10 gating, individual deletion, and clear-all deletion stay in sync with `savedPlayerSelectionIds`.
Keep `선택한 10명 불러오기` disabled unless exactly 10 saved players are checked, and keep save/update available only when the current roster is a valid 10-player match.

When 10 saved players are loaded, repopulate the textarea with canonical TSV, hydrate `matchPlayers`, refresh the current-roster panel, and clear previous candidates/editor until the user recalculates.

milestones.title: Candidate Integration And Verification
milestones.objective: Preserve the existing balance engine and swap editor, but refresh all candidate/editor metadata and tests for the new preference model and saved-player behaviors.
deliverables: Update `src/lib/optimizer.js` and `src/lib/editor.js` so every candidate slot and editor slot carries assigned-role preference fit metadata derived from point values, not rank order.
Keep candidate ordering exactly as specified: total score difference, role-score-difference sum, tank score difference, unranked difference, then random ordering inside fully equal metric buckets.
Do not add role-preference points as a balance ranking key; use them only for slot-level fit metadata and optional compact summaries so tier balance remains the primary decision rule.
Preserve the current result behavior: exactly 6 candidate cards, compact `팀 A / 팀 B` previews, tier color styling, first-candidate auto-load, and immediate two-click swaps.

Update `testing/fakeDom.js` and the existing tests so point editing, save/load, delete flows, exact-10 gating, candidate rendering, and swap recalculation are all executable under the current test harness.

Update `README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` to describe the point-based preference workflow, simplified saved-player list, delete actions, exact-10 loading, and the explicitly non-blocking browser/mobile verification gap for this iteration.

Run `npm test` and `npm run build` as required verification; keep `npm run test:browser` documented as optional evidence when a Chromium-family browser is available, not as a release blocker for this round.

acceptance_criteria: Header-present and headerless 4-column paste input both continue to parse correctly with Korean validation messages.
After paste or saved-player load, the current-roster section shows all 10 active players with editable integer preference controls for `탱커 / 딜러 / 힐러`.
A player with no saved preference data starts at `2 / 2 / 2`.
Every preference edit keeps each role value as an integer and the three-role total exactly `6` at all times.
Saving the current valid roster persists both tier data and preference-point data locally.
Existing saved-player payloads from the old order-based schema load without crashing and are migrated into usable point-based data.
The saved-player panel is a simple name-first list rather than a detailed card grid.
Saved players can be deleted individually from the list.
A clear-all saved-players action removes the entire local saved-player library.
After any delete action, selection counts and exact-10 gating update immediately and no deleted player remains selectable.
`선택한 10명 불러오기` stays disabled unless exactly 10 saved players are selected.
Loading 10 saved players rewrites the textarea with those exact 10 players, hydrates the current-roster section, and clears old candidate/editor results until recalculation.
After valid current players exist, the app still renders exactly 6 candidate combinations.
Every candidate still satisfies `1탱 2딜 2힐` per team and never duplicates a player within that candidate.
Candidate ordering still follows total score difference, role-score-difference sum, tank score difference, and unranked difference; only fully equal metric buckets are randomized.
Candidate preview cards remain compact and show both teams with the required tier color styling.
Selecting a candidate still loads that candidate into the final edit area and clears any pending slot selection from a previous edit.
Two slot clicks still swap players immediately, and the destination-slot tier display plus preference-fit display recalculate from the new slot role.
The main result UI still hides personal numeric scores, team total scores, and numeric balance differences by default.
All new preference, save/load, delete, and status copy is presented in Korean.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` match the shipped workflow and explicitly state that browser/mobile smoke evidence is non-blocking for this iteration.
test_strategy: Replace the old preference-order unit tests with point-based tests covering default `2/2/2`, integer normalization, sum-to-6 enforcement, legacy order migration, and assigned-role fit metadata.
Add storage tests for backward-compatible migration, upsert behavior, individual delete, clear-all delete, corrupted JSON fallback, and round-trip persistence of point-based records.
Keep optimizer tests focused on the mandated balance ranking and candidate uniqueness, and add a deterministic RNG stub test to prove only fully equal metric buckets are randomized.
Extend editor tests so swaps assert both destination-role tier recalculation and destination-role preference-fit recalculation under the point-based model.

Expand app-flow and fake-DOM coverage for current-roster point editing, save/update, startup restore, exact-10 gating, load-selected flow, individual delete, clear-all delete, and hidden-score rendering.
Retain parser and render-contract coverage for optional headers, tier color classes, compact previews, and Korean UI copy after the saved-player panel simplification.
Run `npm test` and `npm run build` before handoff; document `npm run test:browser` only if a compatible browser is available, otherwise mark it skipped and non-blocking.

risks.risk: Changing the saved-player schema from order-based preferences to point-based preferences can silently break existing local data or discard user intent.
risks.mitigation: Implement explicit backward-compatible migration in `src/lib/playerStore.js`, add unit tests for legacy payloads, and preserve old preference intent through a deterministic conversion rule instead of resetting everyone blindly.

risks.risk: Naive numeric inputs can temporarily violate the `sum=6` rule and create inconsistent runtime state.
risks.mitigation: Centralize point-edit normalization in one helper and use constrained stepper-style controls or equivalent logic so the application state never stores invalid totals.

risks.risk: Saved-player delete actions can leave stale selection IDs or mismatched UI counts after mutation.
risks.mitigation: Reconcile `savedPlayerSelectionIds` after every save/delete/load mutation and add app-flow tests that verify counts, disabled states, and rendered rows immediately after deletion.

risks.risk: Preference-point work can accidentally leak new numeric balance details into compact previews or the editor, violating the hidden-score requirement.
risks.mitigation: Keep balance metrics internal to optimizer/editor modules and expose only qualitative or preference-specific display metadata in render functions; add regression tests that search rendered HTML for forbidden score labels.

risks.risk: The builder may accidentally promote preference points into the candidate sort order, which would contradict the spec’s mandatory ranking rules.
risks.mitigation: Treat preference points as metadata only, keep ranking logic isolated in `compareCandidateMetrics`/`rankCandidates`, and lock the required ordering with dedicated optimizer regression tests.

risks.risk: The saved-player list simplification can remove too much context and make loading or deleting the wrong player easy.
risks.mitigation: Keep the row layout name-first but include one short secondary summary line or compact chips, plus clear selected-count feedback and explicit delete buttons.

risks.risk: The current fake DOM may miss interactions needed for the new control scheme, causing false confidence from partial tests.
risks.mitigation: Upgrade `testing/fakeDom.js` early for the chosen control events and keep core normalization/storage logic in pure helper modules that can be tested without DOM complexity.

definition_of_done: The existing clipboard parsing, validation, 6-candidate generation, candidate selection, and two-click swap flow still works.
Per-player role preference is now represented as editable integer points across `탱커 / 딜러 / 힐러`, with a guaranteed total of `6` and default `2 / 2 / 2`.
Candidate and editor slot metadata refresh correctly after preference edits, candidate changes, and swaps under the new point-based model.
Saved players can be saved, restored, selected in an exact-10 name-first list, deleted individually, and deleted in bulk.
The required balance ordering and hidden-score UI rules remain intact.
The product remains frontend-only and deployable as a static GitHub Pages-style bundle.
Automated tests cover migration, preference editing, saved-player deletion/load flows, ranking preservation, rendering, and swap recalculation, and both `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` accurately describe the shipped workflow and the non-blocking browser/mobile verification status for this iteration.
open_questions: Assumption: the clipboard format remains exactly the current 4-column TSV, and role-preference points are edited only in the app UI or loaded from saved local records.
Assumption: legacy saved `preferenceOrder` values should migrate to point totals using a deterministic `3 / 2 / 1` mapping so old user intent is preserved as much as possible.
Assumption: valid role-preference values are non-negative integers whose total is always exactly `6`; no fractional values or negative values are supported.

Assumption: the implementation should prefer constrained stepper-style controls or equivalent immediate normalization instead of free-form text fields that can leave the state invalid between keystrokes.
Assumption: role-preference points must not become a new candidate sort key; they are reflected through slot-level fit metadata and editing guidance, not through overriding the balance ranking.
Assumption: the simplified saved-player list may omit the old detailed tier-card layout as long as player names are easy to scan and the user can still select, load, and delete records confidently.

Assumption: deleting saved players affects only the saved library; if one of those players is already loaded into the current match, that current in-memory match remains unchanged until the user reloads or clears it.
Assumption: browser and mobile smoke verification should stay documented in `README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md`, but the absence of new real-browser evidence is not a blocker for this iteration.
